items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Spend is estimated once at 1960 and seeds the campaign's depletion reserve
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11): "For depletion accounting, I would prefer if we retrofit this, and come to a sensible estimate at the very end of digitisation. For generation you are right in that keeping items abstract is best policy." So NO ACCUMULATOR IS ADDED anywhere in the history sim, and sprint 39's closed Empire span is NOT reopened.

WHY IT MATTERS. Ben, 2026-09-11, on what digitisation passes forward: "the main levers we pass are going to be about how much of easily accessible resource has been actually spent." The saturated corporate web forms around what is LEFT.

WHERE IT LANDS IS ALREADY BUILT, AND THIS IS THE ELEGANT PART. `tile_component::resource_remaining` (components.hpp) is a finite reserve, live, drawn down by extraction and tapering output as it empties -- and it is SEEDED AT GENERATION to richness x a reserve factor (tile_generation.cpp). The two economy phases set that seed instead of a constant. Ground worked for centuries hands the campaign a thinner reserve. No new field, no new accumulator, no change to the campaign's extraction loop.

THE PRICE OF RETROFITTING, STATED PLAINLY AND ACCEPTED. An estimate computed once at 1960 can NEVER BE CHECKED against what actually happened, because nothing recorded it. That makes it a STATED FORMULA rather than a measurement. THE FORMULA MUST THEREFORE BE WRITTEN DOWN AS ONE -- named inputs, named arithmetic, in DIGITISATION.md -- or it silently becomes a fudge factor nobody can audit. Writing it down IS the work; an unwritten estimate is the failure mode.

ITS INPUTS ARE THE ABSTRACT ONES THE SIM ALREADY HOLDS: how long ground was held and worked, its `dominant` region class, whether it industrialised and when, and the corridor throughput that ran off it (BL-940).

PARKED UNTIL DIGITISATION IS DESIGNED. DIGITISATION.md is a placeholder by Ben's ruling; this item is filed now so the decision is not lost, and it is NOT sprint 40 work.

items.author: Claude (sprint 42 wave 1 measurements)
items.title: Six harnesses simulate an 80-tick warm start the game no longer runs
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-16 by BL-978 (warm start retired). Each of the six carries `k_warm_ticks = 80` naming `app::pre_game_ticks`, which no longer exists: the settle is phase 6's validation run, 12 ticks (ERAS.md § the settling pass). Their comments were corrected when the constant went; their numbers were not re-read.

WORK: re-read each against the 12-tick settle, decide per harness whether its subject needs the longer history (a trailing-quarters window may legitimately want more than the settle provides — say so in the harness) and record the movement. This is a reading, not a re-pin: where a band moves, report it.

DONE WHEN: no harness names a retired constant; every band that moved is recorded with its cause.

items.author: Claude (sprint 42 wave 1 measurements)
items.title: The determinism digest covers everything generation moves that play reads: seeded sentiment, road tiers, region and nation treasuries, and the Exploration stocks
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-16 by BL-998 (consolidation folds every seat): folding every held seat's stores into the capital at 1200 CE moved the treasury mean from 18.2M to 32.5M and the post-road count from 34 to 59, and EVERY world_determinism digest stayed identical, because the deep digest does not hash `region::treasury`. BL-975 then moved the digest only because `nation_component::treasury` IS hashed — so the seam is half covered, in a way nobody could predict from the outside.

This is the same shape as BL-957 (world digest sees sentiment and roads), which is still open: the contract proves same-seed-same-world only for the fields it hashes, and a treasury-only regression is invisible.

WORK: fold region treasury, the Exploration span's stocks (port, navy, standing army) and the corridor tier counts into the deep digest alongside BL-957's sentiment and roads; one authorised re-bless with the movement described, in its own commit.

DONE WHEN: a deliberate one-region treasury perturbation fails world_determinism (demonstrate locally); the re-bless is authorised.

--- MERGED FROM BL-957 (WORLD_DIGEST_SEES_SENTIMENT_AND_ROADS), 2026-09-16 ---
FOUND 2026-09-14 by sprint 41 T2 (BL-956): moving world setup from 1200 CE grudges and corridors to 1660 ones took sentiment seeding on seed ABCDEF01 to 76 rows off 225 grudges and stamped corridors from 1664 to 2276, and every world_determinism digest stayed digit-identical, because the digest reads neither `world::sentiment` nor road tiers. SCOPE NOW: fold seeded sentiment (sorted pairs and values), road tier per tile or a per-tier tile count per body, region treasury, the Exploration stocks and corridor tier counts into the deep digest - ONE authorised re-bless for all of it, in its own commit. DONE WHEN: a deliberate one-row perturbation of EACH covered field fails world_determinism locally.

items.author: Claude (sprint 42 wave 1 measurements)
items.title: era_world_harness has three failing rows on main and no record says why
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-16 while attributing BL-975's results. At sprint 42's base commit the harness reads 15 passed / 3 failed: R1 (every 0 CE region was founded by year 0), R2 (the 1960 world stays demography-unseeded) and R5 (the 1960 world still industrialises). They are not this sprint's: they pre-date it and nothing in DEVLOG, NEEDS_REVIEW or the backlog records them as a known baseline the way history_sim_harness's R3a2/R3a3 pair is recorded.

WORK: diagnose each. R1 is a founding-schedule question (the span now closes at 1200 while the epoch is 0 CE — a founding dated after the epoch is plausible rather than wrong, in which case the CHECK is stale and says so); R2 and R5 read the two-span arc, which the default epoch never runs, so they may be asserting on a path only `--epoch 1960` exercises. Either fix the code or restate the check, and record whichever it is — an unexplained red teaches the next reader to ignore the harness.

DONE WHEN: era_world_harness is green on main, or each remaining red is named as a baseline in the harness's own header and in DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md's list.

items.author: Claude (housekeeping pass, from NR-864)
items.title: The sweep's creed classifier compares a product against a mean, so consolidators cannot win
items.design:
READING 3 of exploration_sweep calls a culture a consolidator when `consolidator_lean_q > expansion_lean_q`. The two are not on one scale. `consolidator_lean_q = dominion * (1000 - sea_legs) / 1000` is a PRODUCT, so it is at most the smaller factor; `expansion_lean_q = (sea_legs + zeal) / 2` is a MEAN, so it is at least the smaller input. A middling culture (sea 300, zeal 500, dominion 500) reads 350 against 400 and classifies EXPANSIONIST though nothing about it is seafaring. This is BL-318 incommensurability again: the comparison answers a question about arithmetic, not about creeds.

WHY IT MATTERS AND IS NOT COSMETIC. EXPLORATION.md § Two ways to be strong says that if the creed axes do not separate the strategies, the fix is UPSTREAM IN THE EMPIRE PHASE. That is a large conclusion and it must not be drawn from a comparison that could not have come out the other way. On seeds 0-2 all eighteen top-3 entries classified expansionist, consolidator lean 104-190 against expansion lean 610-860.

THE SIM IS ALREADY FIXED; THIS IS THE INSTRUMENT. BL-955 (spend is scored) uses each lean only as a PER-MILLE RANK among the round's living polities, so the two are compared on one scale wherever the sim reads them. Only the sweep's reading still compares raw values.

THE WORK, in order: (1) measure the lean distribution over ALL living polities on the 16-seed parity sweep, not the top 3, so the call is made on the population; (2) classify by RANK within the world - a culture is a consolidator if its consolidator lean is in the top third by that lean, and likewise for expansion, so a culture may be both or neither; (3) consider putting both leans on one form in src/ (both products or both means) if the rank fix leaves the raw values readable anywhere else.

DONE WHEN: reading 3 reports a creed mix that can come out either way, and the sweep prints the lean distribution it classified against so the reader can see the population behind the label.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: The thirteen Digitisation readings are instrumented over a seed spread before any mechanism lands
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § What the phase is judged on lists thirteen readings at 1960 CE, one per opening-map property and beat: density follows cities, cultural stock, advanced chains, live conflict, mixed cities, inequality, far trade, industrialisation, migration, decolonisation, world war (some worlds, never all, never none), war dead (population falls, no region emptied), and catastrophe lean (world-war worlds open with higher aggregate Alarm against Ceiling).

WHY FIRST. The Exploration sprint landed its readings first (BL-937) and it was the reason the frozen-map risk was measurable. Pass 1 grew mechanisms nobody could judge. This phase is designed backwards from its consumer; the readings are that consumer made executable.

DONE WHEN: a harness prints all thirteen over a 16-seed sweep with a spread, not a per-world verdict, and each reading prints n/a honestly until the mechanism it reads exists. Never weaken a reading to pass.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: The Digitisation span runs 1660 → 1960 on the shared engine, taking exploration_output and producing a validated digitisation handoff
items.design:
The fourth span on history_sim, opening where Exploration closes. Its only input is the exploration_output struct (EXPLORATION.md § What this phase hands digitisation); its output is a struct with a validator on the same footing as the Empire and Exploration handoffs, whose fields are DIGITISATION.md § What crosses into play. The Industry tree is the tree invested in, gated behind Exploration's rim.

MEASURE COST FIRST (DIGITISATION.md § Where it will be hard, item 5): 300 years on a region count that grows inside the run, with migration adding per-round work. Report wall-clock per seed against the Exploration span before adding mechanism.

DONE WHEN: world setup reads grudges and corridors from the 1960 handoff where the span ran (the 1660 ones otherwise), the validator runs in production, world_determinism is bit-identical, and history_sim_harness plus exploration_sim_harness stay green.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Large cities build located industry points, spent on rail, mechanised force or works; the remainder is the charter budget
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § Beat 1. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15): three sinks — RAIL (the road ladder's next rung on corridors from the city), MECHANISED FORCE (army and navy stock from industry rather than treasury), WORKS (the city's own yield next round) — and what is unspent at 1960 is the centre's CHARTER BUDGET.

PROPOSED in the doc and carried: one number per population centre, LOCATED (a conqueror takes it); produced from centre scale, fuel within reach (the Industry tree fuel gate), capital paid in from the polity treasury, and Industry tree capacity; the Works fork (State Arsenal spends, Private Works stockpiles) decides the lean as a derived disposition, never a flag.

The spend is an allocation inside the upkeep step, the Exploration idiom (EXPLORATION.md § Force persists now). No term inside the scorer picks a sink for a polity.

DONE WHEN: the industrialisation reading shows industry points unevenly held with the fuel gate visible in who holds them, and both Works-fork sides appear among industrialised polities.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: People and culture shares stream into cities and across borders, and innovation reads urban mass
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § Beat 2. Two streams on one rule: URBANISATION (countryside to a centre in the same polity) and EMIGRATION (a centre to a centre in another polity), pulled by industry-point output at the destination (the sim holds no wage), pushed by depleted or strained ground, war and a lost colony, carried on a line (held corridors; contact, a line that carries people, no war between the pair).

MIGRATION CARRIES CULTURE SHARES, so population centres gain a culture_shares of their own — the substrate for the culture lens (BL-992) and the cultural demand weight (BL-991).

INNOVATION READS URBAN MASS: Industry tree investment reads the population of a polity's largest centres, superlinearly, on the scorer's one shape (trees/TREES.md § The scorer).

OPEN AND MEASURED: where the pull saturates, so the countryside is not emptied.

DONE WHEN: the migration reading shows urban share rising across the span and a cross-border stream in most worlds, and the mixed-cities reading finds checker-qualifying centres concentrated in large ones.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Subjects refuse renewal once they can pay for themselves, and holding one grows dearer as its cities grow
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § Beat 3. Ben, 2026-09-15: "the ability to keep colonies grows harder regardless of whether there is war." Reuses Exploration's tribute-renewal refusal (EXPLORATION.md § A colony is a subject); the refusal score gains the subject's own urban mass and industry points. The overlord's holding cost (garrison upkeep) scales with the subject's population and industry, so the bill grows with no shot fired. NOTHING COUNTS DOWN — no timer, no era flag.

Wars over empire are contests for subjects between powers, on the existing campaign verb. A decolonised polity crosses at 1960 as a nation.

DONE WHEN: the decolonisation reading shows fewer subjects at 1960 than 1660, not zero, with at least one lost without a war in most worlds.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Industrial war kills through conscript dead, displacement and blockade famine, and never empties a region
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, notes): "we really need to ensure that people die when wars happen. It's not good for any regime or polity." Takes MILITARY_HISTORY.md's 2026-09-09 exception route — an authored, visible mechanism, never a battle coefficient — and only for the Digitisation span.

THREE MECHANISMS (PROPOSED in the doc): CONSCRIPT DEAD — mechanised force is raised from population, and losses are drawn back from the raising regions in proportion to what each gave; DISPLACEMENT — war ground pushes an emigration stream toward safe cities (BL-985); BLOCKADE FAMINE — interdicted supply thins a civilian count while it stands, bounded by duration and food.

THE DEAD-REGION LOOP MUST STAY SHUT (MILITARY_HISTORY.md: 258 battles, 258 conquests, one region). No loss falls on the battlefield region by being fought over.

RELATED: NR-866 records that paid heads cost no population today; conscript dead makes force cost people for the first time.

COST FOR THE VICTOR: fewer people, smaller cities, fewer industry points; war weariness lowers cohesion and raises every subject's refusal.

DONE WHEN: the war-dead reading shows every war lowering population somewhere and no region emptied, across 16 seeds.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: A war over empire becomes general when the mutual-defence graph draws in the great powers, and leaves the epoch more Alarmed
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15): a world war is PERMITTED, NEVER FORCED — "we don't force it, but it is not unlikely. So I am happy with seeds that reach either target." And a world that fought one is "more likely to fail our Era 1 catastrophe — nuclear war."

PROPOSED MECHANISM: a contest for a subject draws each power's mutual-defence partners, and theirs in turn; how densely the great powers are bound decides whether a colonial war stays local. No scheduled event, no roll.

THE ERA 1 LINK uses ERAS.md's two scalars and no third: standing mechanised force, grudges from the dead and severed flows seed per-nation Alarm at world setup; none of it adds Ceiling. It is not the rupture (HISTORY.md § Stage 5: averted, not past).

DONE WHEN: the world-war reading finds one in some worlds and not others across 16 seeds (never all, never none), and the catastrophe-lean reading shows higher aggregate Alarm against Ceiling on world-war worlds. If the rate is all or nothing, the fix is the treaty graph's causes, never a clamp on the war.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Great powers back clients in left-behind or decolonised polities, and wars standing at 1960 cross as a province condition
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § 3. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, elicitation): a war standing at the epoch crosses as a STANDING PROVINCE CONDITION — contested ground, interdicted supply, raised ordnance demand, a named patron — resolved by in-world cost, not by an actor choosing moves. NO NEW GRANT: a live nation war would widen AI_OPPONENT.md § 11 and is raised separately if ever wanted.

PROPOSED in the sim: a patron link (a great power paying treasury or force into a client's army), arising where mutual deterrence makes direct war dear — the arms race's next displacement. Nothing picks the client; the price gap does.

WORK SPANS the sim (patron link), the handoff (standing wars and patrons), and the campaign province condition's effect on supply and ordnance demand.

DONE WHEN: the live-conflict reading shows a standing condition in most worlds, most on left-behind or decolonised ground, and a player can see the condition and its patron on the planetary canvas.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: The landscape search spends each city's charter budget, so firm density follows cities
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, elicitation): Digitisation decides HOW MUCH and WHERE; the search decides WHICH. The search is Digitisation's last act (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Round 5 note; DIGITISATION.md § This phase sets budgets; the search spends them). CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 6 is amended forward: breadth decides which goods a firm serves, the budget decides how many firms stand where.

OWED AND MEASURED: how a budget converts to a firm count, and whether it is spent whole. MEASURE AGAINST TICK COST before tuning density for the map — a dense web is many actors running the corporate scorer every tick.

DONE WHEN: the density reading shows firm count per market rising with catchment urban population rather than good count, and a campaign tick at the seeded density is measured and reported.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Household demand keeps universal presence and takes a cultural weight from the catchment's peoples
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, elicitation): MARKETS.md § Three properties the set has to hold, property 5, AMENDED — every market keeps a buyer for every terminal good its band supports; the VOLUME of household demand for a good is weighted by the population-weighted preference of the culture shares across the catchment (region and centre shares). Preference is Exploration's derived per-culture weight, carried to 1960.

ALSO SEEDED HERE: the starting price per market from the scarcity signal, inside the band (DIGITISATION.md Part III).

DONE WHEN: the cultural-stock reading shows the most-preferred goods with a local or preferred seller in most markets, and two markets on one world show different household demand for the same good for a reason the culture lens can show.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: A culture lens fills provinces with the primary culture and checkers the second where it is within 95%
items.design:
LENSES.md § Culture lens. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15): primary culture per province as a blended lineage-hue fill; a HARD CHECKER of the top two where the second share is at least 95% OF THE FIRST (relative: 42/40 checkers, 42/38 does not). Only the top two draw. The checker is the one exception to PROVINCES.md § Every lens blends across provinces.

DATA: province culture is DERIVED (PROVINCES.md § What a province is, amended) — region rural shares blended with each inside centre's shares, population-weighted; nothing stored on the province. Reuses palette::lineage_colour (BL-919).

QUESTION (required on every surface): "Who lives here, and so what does this market want?" — add the question_log entry and the ui_elements row.

DONE WHEN: a verifier-visual capture shows plain countryside and checkered cities on a Digitisation world, AND a live click in the built app arms the lens and reads a checkered province (a UI requirement needs a live check).

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Nations read GDP, markets read listed value, and inequality reads as spreads between nations and cities
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, elicitation). GDP (NATIONS.md § GDP): valued production on a nation's tiles at local prices, derived, trailing window in play, capacity at the seeded price field at the epoch; promotes NR-774's tool-only definition. LISTED VALUE (MARKETS.md § A market's listed value): summed buyout valuation of firms headquartered in the catchment — a sum over firms, no equity, no share price. INEQUALITY: GDP per head across nations and output per centre within one, read never stored, never households.

One shared implementation for the harness reading and the player surface, so a check never measures something different from the screen.

DONE WHEN: the inequality reading shows wide spreads on both axes, and the nation and market surfaces show GDP and listed value with a live click.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: The epoch seeds stub campaign tech, a regime field and garrison strength from the Digitisation handoff
items.design:
DIGITISATION.md § 6, SET (Ben, 2026-09-15): "very simple stubs for now." TECH: the Industry tree mask sets the campaign tree's starting unlocks per nation (The Renewed Line opens it). REGIME: one field beside the three character enums, derived from the Works fork, charter reach, subject history and whether the polity fought a world war; invented names only. GARRISONS: sized from carried army_stock, navy and mechanised force, not from a treasury seeded at zero.

Stubs mean one field each with a named source; nothing reads the regime in play yet.

DONE WHEN: two nations on one world open with different tech state, regime and garrison strength traceable to their history, and the save round-trips the new fields.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, trade and demand design form); Claude (written into POPULATION, MARKETS, SUPPLY, PRODUCTION)
items.title: Auto-dispatch is the seller chasing a net price, bounded by what the gap absorbs, for every corp including the player
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, form). SUPPLY.md § Dispatch trigger owns the rule.

For every (corp, market) pool holding a good above its processor reservation, using last tick's prices: net(d) = price_d - haul_per_unit(src->d) - handling_per_unit - duty_per_unit(d); send to argmax_d net(d) (ties lower market id) if net(d) - price_src > margin_threshold x price_src. Quantity = min(surplus, q) less what the corp already has in transit to d, where q = supply_d x ((price_d / landed_cost)^2 - 1) from the sqrt price law; a destination with zero supply absorbs its unmet demand. The threshold is authored in data, measured, never zero. The shortfall scan is RETIRED — a short market prices high, so the rule reaches it.

ONE RULE FOR EVERY CORP, THE PLAYER'S INCLUDED; the player keeps hold_convoy and the directed verb. The rival scorer's directed-dispatch valuation (corp_ai.cpp:2068-2072, qty x dest_price - leg.cost) subtracts the home price too.

WHY: the shortfall trigger never read a price, so a seller never moved goods toward a better market. With per-market pools (BL-1003) and cheap sea legs (BL-1004) this is property 7 of DIGITISATION.md.

DONE WHEN: convoy_command asserts the directed verb and auto-dispatch price a leg identically; a harness row shows a seller sending to a farther higher-priced market over a nearer cheaper one; no destination receives more in one tick than its q; and the far-trade reading (BL-1006) shows a material share of delivered volume skipping the nearest market after a year of play.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, trade and demand design form); Claude (written into POPULATION, MARKETS, SUPPLY, PRODUCTION)
items.title: Household demand follows headcount up cumulative stratum rungs, upper rungs scaled by qualification, and an unmet top rung blocks promotion
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, form). POPULATION.md § The stratum ladder owns it.

(1) SIZE BY HEADCOUNT, RENORMALISED: volume = heads / heads_per_demand_unit x basket[r] x elasticity. The constant is DERIVED from the generated centre distribution so world household demand at generation equals the tier-index total (on generation weights 40/30/20/8/2 and rungs 10k..5M: 239k heads over 2.02 scale points, ~118k heads a unit); recorded with its derivation, re-derived when rungs or distribution move, held fixed in play. A metropolis is 500x a village, not 5x.

(2) CUMULATIVE RUNGS, industrial band: 1 staples (food rations, agricultural produce, water); 2 clean water, medical supplies; 3 consumer goods; 4 refined fuel; 5 electronics. Volumes measured against the recipe-margin anchor. Ancient rungs PROPOSED in the doc.

(3) QUALIFICATION SCALES RUNGS 4-5, normalised to the world mean at generation. Staples and welfare do not scale.

(4) AN UNMET TOP RUNG BLOCKS PROMOTION (the sustained-met-supply precondition made specific).

(5) STOPGAP: electronics leaves inject_background_demand (the metropolis rung buys it); silicon, refined copper, REE alloy, machinery, alloys stay, labelled stopgap, until building upkeep buys them.

DEFECT FOLDED IN (found 2026-09-15): inject_background_demand grants each market its whole body's population total, so demand multiplies with market count (market_clearing.cpp:294-348) and razed centres are not skipped. Split the body pull across markets by catchment population; skip razed centres.

Cultural weight (BL-991) composes on top.

DONE WHEN: demand_census shows electronics with a household buyer in metropolis-scale markets with the stopgap no longer carrying it; the heads_per_demand_unit derivation is printed and world household demand at generation matches the tier-index total within rounding; a centre with its top rung unmet does not promote in a harness row; background demand on a nine-market body equals, not nine-folds, its population pull.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, Digitisation design session, elicitation form and notes); Claude (written into DIGITISATION.md and siblings)
items.title: Wizard round 6 is a 1660 → 1960 time-lapse of the three beats that closes on the seeded opening map
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, elicitation): STARTUP.md § Rounds, round 6 — a time-lapse on the same 2D map as rounds 3–5 showing industrialisation (cities lighting, rail spreading), mass migration (streams into cities, their culture tint turning mixed) and decolonisation (subjects standing up, wars over empire flaring, one sometimes general), closing on the epoch's opening map with firms and the market carve drawn in place. Replaces the placeholder and the still-globe specification.

Same contract as rounds 3–5: write-only tap, playhead lags the calculation at a constant rate (~30 s span), scrubbable once landed, causal reroll, no Run button.

DONE WHEN: a live click through the wizard reaches round 6, watches the three beats and lands on the seeded map, and a watched and unwatched run are byte-identical.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, trade and demand design form); Claude (written into POPULATION, MARKETS, SUPPLY, PRODUCTION)
items.title: Goods pools are keyed per (corp, market), so a same-body haul delivers and sells where it arrives
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, form: pools per market over a consignment). PRODUCTION.md § Stockpile and output flow owns it; MARKETS.md § Market centres and seeding and SUPPLY.md § Convoy entity amended.

DEFECT IT FIXES (found 2026-09-15): pools are keyed (corp, body) (world.hpp:272, :701-703); commit_convoy debits pool_for(corp, src_body) (supply_system.cpp:660) and arrival credits pool_for(corp, dest_body) (:182-183) — the same pool on one body — and auto-surplus then sells through market_for_corp_on_body, the lowest-id building's market (market_clearing.cpp:206-221). Every same-body market-to-market haul paid haulage and sold back at home. haulage_measure's 1614 same-body hauls measured dispatch, never trade.

THE RULE: a building's output enters the pool of market_for_tile(building tile); its inputs draw that pool plus that market's inventory; wants, purchases, auto-surplus, standing orders and the running remainder key (corp, market). A body with no market keeps one body-level pool until its first building spawns one. Labour pools stay (corp, body).

COSTS, STATED: save format (save_game_version moves, round-trip assertion owed per NR-708); state_hash folds the new key in sorted order; a roster straddling a catchment line now needs hauls, so the landscape search must score it — measure how many generated firms straddle before and after.

DONE WHEN: a harness hauls a good between two markets on one body and the goods sell at the destination price; world_determinism bit-identical across runs; save round-trips pools; the landscape search winner still validates.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, trade and demand design form); Claude (written into POPULATION, MARKETS, SUPPLY, PRODUCTION)
items.title: A water-crossing route is land, sea and land legs; sea is cheapest per distance and every port charges handling
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, form). SUPPLY.md § Logistical cost and § Infrastructure gates own it.

ORDERING PER DISTANCE: sea < land at its best road tier (today land 0.02 x highway 0.40 = 0.008 against sea 0.05 — reversed). Values measured; the ordering is the ruling. HANDLING: a per-unit fee at each port a cargo passes through, independent of distance, so a short coastal hop loses to a road and a long crossing wins. REPORT THE CROSSOVER DISTANCE whenever either term moves.

PER-LEG ROUTING replaces the whole-route crosses_ocean bit (logistics.cpp:223-225, :308; supply_system.cpp:513-527; formerly BL-522, purged): land source->port A, sea A->B, land B->destination, ports chosen to minimise total including both fees; each leg at its own speed (caravan 25 km/day, coastal 130). A sea leg runs only port to port; source and destination markets may be inland.

RE-DERIVE the price ceiling input (MARKETS.md § Where the ceiling comes from) with haulage_measure on per-leg costs.

DONE WHEN: a harness route across water prices as three legs with two handling fees; a long crossing beats the land detour and a short hop does not; haulage_measure re-run and its table updated; convoy_command still asserts directed and auto legs agree.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, trade and demand design form); Claude (written into POPULATION, MARKETS, SUPPLY, PRODUCTION)
items.title: Import duty is charged when a convoy arrives across a border, paid by the shipper, replacing the matched-trade charge
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, form). MARKETS.md § Tariffs — the first flow that pays a nation owns it.

On arrival, if the destination market's nation differs from the source market's nation, the convoy owner pays qty x destination last-resolved price x the destination nation's import_tariff rate (law.cpp:214-234, stacked, clamped [0,1]) to that nation's treasury, as a transfer in one statement. Same-nation hauls and markets with no nation (off-world) pay nothing. The matched-order-book charge (market_clearing.cpp:1257-1291) is RETIRED so no good pays twice.

WHY: the old charge fired only on matched trades whose buy side has no emitter in play, so no tariff ever fired and seeded protection (law.hpp:247-254) shaped nothing.

DONE WHEN: money_conservation asserts the duty is a transfer and that a no-tariff world stays hash-identical; a harness row shows a cross-border convoy paying and a same-nation convoy not.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-15, trade and demand design form); Claude (written into POPULATION, MARKETS, SUPPLY, PRODUCTION)
items.title: One reading measures delivered volume sold at its destination and the share that skipped the seller's nearest market, after a year of play
items.design:
LANDS FIRST, before BL-1003/1004/1005/995, the way the Digitisation and Exploration readings did: a mechanism with no reading cannot be judged.

MEASURES, on the landscape-search winner over a seed spread, at the epoch and again after four quarterly ticks x N (a year of play): (a) volume DELIVERED and SOLD at a destination market other than the source pool's market — not dispatch count; (b) the share of that volume whose destination is not the seller's nearest market; (c) the price gap per delivered good at dispatch and at arrival, so a gap play erases is visible.

RE-READS the recorded 1614 same-body hauls honestly: under per-body pools they deliver zero, and the reading must say so on today's tree.

DONE WHEN: the reading prints all three on today's tree (expected ~0 for (a) same-body) and is named in the gate list for BL-1003, BL-1004 and BL-995.

items.title: Research points accrue from population - the parked placeholder, stated as one

items.author: The sprint 35 step 4a review barrier (2026-09-08); Claude
items.title: A holder with no free culture slot loses its assimilation into the anonymous tail
items.design:
FOUND BY THE STEP 4a REVIEW BARRIER. It silently disables the anti-hegemony lever BL-826 exists to build, on exactly the ground where that lever matters most.

THE PATH. All three named slots hold A, B, C; a fourth culture D takes the region. shift_toward(D, ...) finds no slot for D (settlement.cpp:96), the displacement test taken > cw[smallest] fails while the smallest slot is bigger than one round's take, and line 112 puts the gain into other_q. share_of(D) reads the TAIL as 0, so the w_cult term (history_sim.cpp:1190) charges D the FULL foreign discount forever. The ground never digests.

AND THE ACCUMULATED GAIN IS PERMANENTLY LOST. When D finally does claim a slot it restarts from one round's take; the reviewer measured roughly 240 per-mille of assimilation stranded in a tail that is foreign to every culture and never re-attributed. The tail is documented as "peoples too small to name"; this path makes it a one-way sink for the HOLDER'S OWN share.

THIS IS THE COMMON CASE, NOT A CORNER. A frontier region changing hands three times is ordinary - and on the current fixture one region changes hands 258 times (BL-835).

SHAPE OF A FIX, not prescribed: the holder's share is the one share that must be nameable, since it is the one every downstream reader asks about. Either the holder always claims a slot on first gain, or the tail tracks the holder separately from the anonymous remainder. Whichever, the invariant to state and then assert is that a share the sim is actively accruing is never written somewhere share_of cannot read it back.

DONE WHEN: a holder with three foreign slots digests its ground at the same rate as one with a free slot, and a harness asserts no accrued share is unreadable.

items.author: The sprint 35 step 4a review barrier (2026-09-08); Claude
items.title: Integer truncation freezes small grudges forever, falsifying both decay and sparsity
items.design:
FOUND BY THE STEP 4a REVIEW BARRIER. Two of the grudge design's stated properties are false in the code, and both were argued for in prose rather than measured.

THE ARITHMETIC. g.score -= (g.score * shed) / 1000 (history_sim.cpp:770) truncates to a ZERO decrement once score < 1000/shed. shed = grudge_decay_per_year_q (3) x step_years, so in the -20..0 band (step 5) shed is 15 and any score below 67 decrements by exactly nothing, forever. At the 4000-year span the -400..-100 band (step 20, shed 60) freezes everything below 17; the -100..-20 band (step 10, shed 30) freezes everything below 34.

SO A SINGLE border_raided (magnitude 60) raised late in a run is frozen at 60 for the rest of it. It never reaches grudge_floor (4), so it is never erased, and it crosses the handoff as a permanent row.

BOTH DESIGN CLAIMS FALL. The comment's "a half-life near 230 years, so a single old wrong is gone by the epoch" is true only for LARGE scores. And the sparse table the design is built on is not sparse: every pair that ever skirmished keeps a permanent row. Sparsity was one of the three reasons the ledger was affordable at 4000 years.

The usual fix is a minimum decrement of one where score is above the floor, but that changes the half-life at the bottom of the range and should be measured rather than assumed.

DONE WHEN: no score above grudge_floor is stationary across a round at any step_years in use, and a 4000-year run's grudge count is measured rather than asserted.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, the sprint 39 design session: the colonial round sets the demand, the corporations come after); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A polity may buy a province across water for trade, keeping its customs - the diplomatic claim beside the military one
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09: "By diplomatic, I meant something like purchasing a province for the purpose of trade, and respecting local customs. The alternative would be military claims, and war for items such as gold."

TWO CLAIM VERBS, ONE CONTEST. The campaign verb across a sea leg is BL-832's; this item adds PURCHASE: a polity pays for a province out of the stores its seat accumulates (CIVILISATION.md § Materials are spent - the same currency, no second one) and gains ACCESS - the province's endowment becomes reachable to the buyer's network. It does not gain the people: A PURCHASED PROVINCE KEEPS ITS CULTURE SHARES. That is "respecting local customs" as data, and it is what makes the map readable afterwards - bought and taken differ in the shares and in the grudge ledger, and a player can point at either.

THE SCORER CHOOSES ON THE GROUND'S TERMS, never on a posture flag: rich metal behind weak defence scores the campaign; a cash-crop province under a polity with full stores scores the purchase; an empty-stored seller is cheaper to buy from.

THE GRANT. Same actor, same grain, same constraints as the 2026-08-18 nation-and-polity grant - but RAISED rather than read into the existing verbs, because a verb that creates a relationship is the shape the standing rule says to raise. Recorded in AI_OPPONENT.md § 11 on 2026-09-09.

OPEN, and measured rather than chosen: what a purchase costs, and whether the seller's price rises with what its stores hold. A number picked to make one seed buy is the wrong number.

DONE WHEN: purchases happen across water on a seeded sweep alongside campaigns, the sweep reports the bought/taken split per world and it is not degenerate, purchased provinces' culture shares are unmoved by the purchase, and history_sweep prints the distribution.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, the sprint 39 design session: the colonial round sets the demand, the corporations come after); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The colonial tie is a sea lane stamped from the record, read by everything that reads traversal cost
items.design:
THE FINDING THAT CHANGED THE DESIGN. The earlier reading seeded the order book's preferred-seller relationships from colonial ties. MARKETS.md § Where the order book lives: the buy side is engine-only, no press and no corp_verb submits a buy order, so preferred-seller routing is dormant in play. A tie landing there would be a relationship nothing reads - not a force. Ben's call on the form (2026-09-09): the tie is a HAULAGE DISCOUNT on the metropole-colony route.

THE SHAPE IS § 4a ONE LEVEL DOWN. The colonial era RECORDS every sea leg it walked - a purchase party's crossing, a campaign's sea supply, the standing traffic between a metropole and what it holds - run-length counted like the corridors BL-768 records; a pass after it STAMPS the legs onto water tiles as a SEA LANE tier that discounts the sea-leg traversal cost in LOGISTICS.md § 1. Traffic earns the tier; a crossing made once is no lane. Purely additive and purely water. LOGISTICS.md § 4b owns it.

WHAT READS IT is everything that reads tile_traversal_cost, because § 1 is one weight function: convoys (a colony's chains close through its metropole FIRST because the landed price says so), the reach-field Dijkstra, and PLACEMENT REACH (§ 3) - so a firm on one shore may legally hold a site on the other. That second effect is wider than a market preference and is intended: a tie only prices could see would be invisible to the corporate search, which reads reach cost (BL-812, phase 6 sees roads).

DETERMINISM DIGEST: this changes traversal cost on every generated world that has a lane, so world_determinism's digests are re-blessed deliberately, once, with the description of what changed - and seedA/off (no prehistory) must be byte-identical, which is the control.

OPEN: whether a lane decays when its traffic stops. Roads do not; the sea is not a roadbed.

DONE WHEN: lanes stamp on 4 of 4 seeds where the colonial record has repeat crossings, the sea-leg cost census shows the discount on lane tiles and nowhere else, seedA/off is unmoved, and the lanes render on the planetary canvas and in round 5.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, the sprint 39 design session: the colonial round sets the demand, the corporations come after); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: How wealthy a nation is - a per-polity wealth scalar over 1560-1960 that seeds the opening treasury and the endemic channel's wealth term
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09: the colonial round tells you "how wealthy certain nations are, and furthers the global wealth inequality for the next phase."

THE SHAPE IS protection_q's (BL-750): a scalar per polity computed in ONE block at the end of the span, after the loop, read by nothing inside it - so it is a DERIVED output and never a scored verb. Moved deterministically by facts the span already accumulates: furnace timing against neighbours (the axis the tariff posture reads), endemic sources reached (BL-877), provinces bought (BL-875) and spoils of provinces taken (BL-832), lanes kept open (BL-876).

WHERE IT LANDS: the nation's opening treasury balance (NATIONS.md § 2 The treasury) and the wealth term the endemic channel scales its want by. Nothing else; wealth here is not a price, a market or a firm.

THE SPREAD IS THE DELIVERABLE. GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Asymmetry is the deliverable forbids clamping any start; this is where the inequality it asks for is FURTHERED. No Gini target. history_sweep reports the distribution per seed and asserts only that it is not degenerate - a flat spread is the ONLY trigger for reweighting the terms.

OPEN: the composition, term by term, and whether spoils should outweigh access. A measurement, not a judgement.

DONE WHEN: every nation opens with a treasury the scalar seeded, the sweep prints the per-world spread and it is wide with real tails, and the tariff and endemic passes read the same scalar rather than re-deriving one.

items.author: Claude (review-queue resolution, 2026-09-16)
items.title: An empty culture folds back into its parent at the boundary, keeping the lineage link
items.design: BEN'S CALL (2026-09-16, NR-879, option A): fold, do not stop coining. THE MEASUREMENT (BL-968 step 1, 16 seeds): 5,453 cultures coined, 790 hold ground when the Empires round opens (14.4%), 471 still hold at 1200 CE (8.6%). The empty mass is overwhelmingly first-generation daughters -- 4,455 empty leaves against 208 empty interior nodes -- and no cradle is ever empty. THE WORK. At the Colonisation/Empires boundary, a culture holding no ground folds into its parent; the lineage link is KEPT, so the tree still reads as a descent rather than losing a generation. Empty INTERIOR nodes need re-parenting -- their children survive and must not be orphaned -- which is the half that makes this a 4 and not a 2. WHY FOLD RATHER THAN GATE: Ben chose the option that keeps the coining rule untouched, so the split counters, the tails and the palette all still see every split that happened; what shrinks is only the set of names that outlive it. THE TREE SHRINKS ABOUT 85% AND EVERY DIGEST MOVES -- a wave re-bless is required, with this item as its named cause (DELIVERY.md section The digest re-bless). DONE WHEN: the lineage palette, kinship years, culture opposition and the Empires round polity seeding all walk a tree whose leaves are names somebody lived under; empty interior nodes are re-parented with no orphan; and the reading that found this reports the post-fold holding fraction.

items.author: Claude (review-queue resolution, 2026-09-16)
items.title: visible_capability_reference is re-scaled so alarm discriminates between near pairs instead of reading 1000 everywhere
items.design: BEN'S CALL (2026-09-16, NR-880): re-scale alarm FIRST, then file the first-crossing question (BL-1019). THE FINDING (BL-999, 16 seeds): visible_capability_reference = 5000 saturates, so alarm reads 1000 on essentially every near pair on every seed, and the deterrence weight acts as a FLAT CONSTANT rather than a discriminator. THIS IS CHEAP AND IT GOES FIRST because it makes every later deterrence reading mean something: the arms-race constant tuned in sprint 41 was tuned against a saturated signal, so no reading taken through it has been discriminating. THE WORK. Pick the reference off the MEASURED distribution of visible capability rather than a round number, so the alarm curve spends its range where the pairs actually sit. NOT A TARGET: the reference is set from the distribution, never tuned until a downstream figure looks right -- the project's standing refusal to fit a figure to a target applies exactly here. DONE WHEN: alarm across near pairs has a spread rather than a mode at 1000, the sweep reports that spread, and the sprint-41 arms-race reading is RE-TAKEN through the unsaturated signal and recorded (whatever it then says). Digests move; this is a named re-bless cause.

items.author: Claude (review-queue resolution, 2026-09-16)
items.title: Why four of six held seeds meet exactly one polity in 460 years, and what opens a frontier
items.design: BEN'S CALL (2026-09-16, NR-880): file the first crossing as its own item, after the alarm re-scale (BL-1018). THE READING (BL-999, 16 seeds): seeds 0, 3, 6 and 7 have NO FRONTIER -- by 1660 each has met exactly ONE polity across a landmass. Tens of thousands of unmet candidates reach the scorer each run, 2-8% clear the threshold, and one or two are ever chosen in 460 years. WHY IT MATTERS: displacement is the Exploration phase's one STRUCTURAL claim, and these seeds are not failures of deterrence -- there is no frontier to displace onto in the first place. THE IMPLICATED CONSTANTS, named by the census: the campaign threshold, and the PRIZE PRICING FOR AN UNMET TARGET (a target nobody has met is priced on what is known about it, which is nothing, so it loses every ranking to a known neighbour). DEPENDS ON BL-1018 -- read nothing here through a saturated alarm signal. ALSO IN SCOPE, from the same census: seed 12 fits none of the four labels (91% of its near pairs are treaty-bound, and the four unbound pairs carry 51% of allowed near campaigns against the frontier's 0.9%), so the label set needs either a fifth entry or a widened DETERRENCE-INERT. DONE WHEN: a seed that meets one polity in 460 years is either explained as correct for its geography or is no longer the common case, and the sweep reports first-contact count per seed so the claim is measured rather than argued.

items.author: Claude (review-queue resolution, 2026-09-16)
items.title: The seat viability floor reads the static landscape score, not eight quarters of trailing net
items.design: BEN'S CALL (2026-09-16, NR-881, option 3): the floor is measuring the wrong thing for a world that has not traded yet, and it should read the static score instead. THE SYMPTOM (BL-978, a Release run): "shortlist 0 of 8 specialists -- VIABILITY FLOOR UNMET". The warm start is gone; the settle is phase 6's single validation run of 12 ticks, chosen as the first tick at which the 4- and 8-tick trailing convoy means are both within 5% of the settled level. The floor reads solvency plus trailing net over EIGHT QUARTERS, and over ticks 5 to 12 the field is still ramping, so nothing clears it. WHY NOT SHORTEN THE WINDOW (the cheap option Ben declined): the 2026-08-26 record says most corps were underwater at 80 ticks too, so a shorter window would re-read the same wrong quantity and would likely still be empty -- the settle is not long enough for a TRADING record to exist at all, at any window. THE WORK. The shortlist ranks and gates on the static landscape score the search already computed for the seat (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md section The eight phases, phase 6) -- a property of the ground, its reach and its market, which is exactly what is knowable before the first convoy runs. Trailing net stays as DISPLAYED information on the seat card; it stops being the gate. THE PLAYER-FACING POINT: the player picks a seat from this shortlist, so an empty shortlist is a broken opening, not a tuning nit. DONE WHEN: a live Release run seats a non-empty shortlist on the 16 curated seeds, and the seat card still shows the trailing figures it no longer gates on.

items.author: Claude (review-queue resolution, 2026-09-16)
items.title: Trade income is paid on the distinct unlike classes a realm can reach, not on roaded pairs
items.design: BEN'S CALL (2026-09-16, NR-827, option 2): re-base trade on something that scales with a realm, then re-measure. THE MEASUREMENT (BL-895, 16 seeds at --epoch 0, both sinks live): production fell 241,000,000 -> 113,922,140 per world and the three sinks claimed 63% of it, but TRADE is 281,280 of that -- 0.25%. What makes war affordable is industry, not the network. WHY THE MECHANISM AND NOT THE CONSTANT: a per-link constant can never grow with a realm the way industry does, because the number of unlike PAIRS a realm touches is bounded by its adjacency. Raising trade_income_per_link until the share looked material would be fitting a figure to a target, which this project refuses (and Ben declined option 3, cutting industry's yield, for the same reason). THE NEW BASE: how many DISTINCT unlike trade classes the realm can reach, not how many roaded pairs it holds. That still reads only DIFFERENCE, so the no-market constraint of the Era -1 sim is intact, and it grows with a realm because reaching further reaches more KINDS of ground. DONE WHEN: BL-895's own "done when" is met -- a polity connected to unlike ground sustains campaigns a disconnected one cannot -- measured, not argued; and the re-measured trade share is RECORDED WHATEVER IT IS, including if the honest answer turns out to be that trade is still minor in this phase.

items.author: Claude (review-queue resolution, 2026-09-16)
items.title: Measure the cost of taking coastal ground against inland ground before any sea-legs magnitude moves
items.design: BEN'S CALL (2026-09-16, NR-828): measure first, tune nothing yet. THE FINDING (BL-899, 16 seeds against a sea_legs_ration_q=0 control): the spectrum is live in the code -- ration = sea_legs_ration_q * legs / 1000, so a people at the floor lands on 270 per-mille and one at full legs on 900 -- but of the 405 wet crossings that actually LAUNCH, ZERO starve. Every hub that clears the port and can_field_naval gates also clears the sea-legs floor of 300, so the floor is REDUNDANT WITH THE PORT GATE rather than discriminating on its own. The discrimination that makes "most peoples cannot cross" true happens upstream at the BL-778 legality gate (median 969 wet contacts refused per world). THE QUESTION THIS ITEM ANSWERS, and it is the only thing in scope: 900 is close enough to full forage that the inversion Ben rejected -- coastal ground becoming CHEAPER to take than inland ground -- is worth testing directly rather than assumed absent. THE WORK IS A READING, NOT A CHANGE. Compare the cost of taking coastal ground against inland ground across the sweep. IF COASTAL IS NOT CHEAPER, the honest outcome is that nothing changes and the redundancy is legitimate -- say so in CREEDS.md and close. If it IS cheaper, that is a new call for Ben with a number attached. NEITHER MAGNITUDE MOVES TO MAKE A NUMBER LOOK RIGHT.

items.author: Claude (review-queue resolution, 2026-09-16)
items.title: A fifth Colonisation branch, Forest, teaches woodland and boreal; arid and stone stay hostile country
items.design: BEN'S CALL (2026-09-16, NR-819, option B -- the deeper option, and the cap has room). THE PROBLEM: classify_farm_class yields TWELVE classes (boreal, volcanic, floodplain, montane, coastal, woodland, arid, valley, highland, grassland, stone, steppe) and the tree folds them into FOUR ground families -- Wet Ground (floodplain, valley), High Ground (highland, montane, volcanic), Open Ground (grassland, steppe), The Shore (coastal) -- leaving woodland, boreal, arid and stone belonging to no branch. A people coined on unowned ground climbs the spire on contact alone, which makes it uniformly poor by accident rather than by design. THE WORK. A fifth branch, FOREST, for woodland and boreal, costing about seven nodes. Arid and stone stay UNOWNED DELIBERATELY -- hostile country that teaches nothing is a design statement once it is written down, and the doc must say so explicitly so the next reader does not file this same question again. A fifth branch re-shapes the tree: rule 4 breadth and the milestone requires_any sets both move (trees/TREES.md owns the grammar). ALSO IN SCOPE: the gate vocabulary has no highland atom, so High Ground's majors carry no gate; add the atom if the sweep shows High Ground nodes held by peoples who never stood on high ground, and say so in the item record either way. CHEAP NOW, EXPENSIVE AFTER BL-882. DONE WHEN: a table in COLONISATION_TREE.md names which class teaches which branch for all twelve, tree_lint is green on doc and store together, and the sweep shows Forest nodes held by forest peoples.

items.title: Raise the colonisation span region count and accept a multi-minute watched wait in round 4
items.design: BEN'S CALL (2026-09-16, NR-809, option 3): raise the region count anyway and accept the wait, on the grounds STARTUP.md already states -- a watched wait needs no budget (Ben, 2026-09-08), and the wait IS the content. THIS IS THE OPTION THAT COSTS WALL CLOCK AND BUYS RESOLUTION, chosen over capping at 2,500-3,000 and over re-modelling adjacency. THE MEASUREMENT (history_span_cost, /O2, seeds 0 and 1, taken AFTER BL-844): reach is QUADRATIC in regions -- exponent 1.95-2.27 on seed 0 and 2.13-2.27 on seed 1 -- and reach is 24-37% of the whole run. Seed 1's 4,000-year run (6,541 ms total, 1,546 ms reach) would spend roughly 400 SECONDS in reach alone at sixteen times the regions. BL-844 already spent the cheap fix: the heapless scan's quadratic is gone and what remains is the NEIGHBOUR GRAPH DENSIFYING as regions fill in -- a property of the graph, not the algorithm, so no further heap work touches it. WHAT THIS ITEM MUST ACTUALLY DO, and it is not "change a constant": pick the new count by MEASURING what round 4 costs at each step up, and stop where the watched wait stops being watchable rather than where a target says. The wait is only content if something is DRAWN during it -- the rounds already draw as the pass computes (BL-820, delivered), so check the round still MOVES at the higher count - a playhead parked at the frontier for minutes is a blank progress bar with better art. DONE WHEN: the round 4 wall clock at the chosen count is recorded in the item, the arc Ben named as the acceptance test still reads (origin, communication, conquest or union, a stable dark age), and the wait draws.

items.title: Round 4's world is cached and handed to Begin, so the second full build is skipped
items.design: BEN'S CALL (2026-09-16, NR-811, option 2): cache the world rather than accept the double build. THE DEFECT, raised as a novelty flag by the BL-829 implementer rather than assumed acceptable: to obtain one recorded history pass, round 4's worker runs make_hard_coded_world and THROWS THE WORLD AWAY, keeping only the record. Pressing Begin at the end of the wizard then builds the world AGAIN. Roughly 73 seconds twice, in Debug. WHY THE CURRENT SHAPE EXISTS, and it must not be undone: it uses generation's own single invocation, and the alternative of re-deriving settlement and the era inside the UI layer is precisely the drift era_minus_one.hpp exists to stop (the seventh-caller defect NR-733 closed). THE WORK. The wizard holds a WORLD rather than a record, and Begin takes it. This is a bigger change than it sounds -- it moves ownership of a large object into the wizard's lifetime, and the failure modes are a stale world surviving a control move that should invalidate it, and the memory cost of holding one while the wizard is open. Both need stating in STARTUP.md, because a cached world that does not match the controls is worse than a slow one. MEASURE RELEASE FIRST: the 73 s figure is Debug, and build and build_rel timings are not comparable -- record the Release figure in the item before choosing how much machinery this deserves. DONE WHEN: Begin does not rebuild, a control move that changes the world invalidates the cache, and STARTUP.md states the ownership and the invalidation rule.
